summary: structcore is the derived, regenerate-never-maintain structural index: a multi-language walk/parse/clone/import-graph builder (index.py) with layered lenses on top (typegraph = Type plane, markdown = Knowledge plane, artifacts = Data plane, forest/lpg = the Project-Twin IR and its LPG projection, dss = deterministic context selection, slice = the token-reducing retrieval product). It is the most heavily wired subsystem in the repo: 21 distinct daedalus modules import it, ~37 test files cover it, and the recent gardener distillates (G-01 fan_in alias-split, G-02 center: directive + root .daedalusignore, G-03 junction guard) are real, TDD'd, measured correctness fixes to the identity layer. Overall health is high for correctness and honesty (every degradation is reported, never silent) and weak for ergonomics: the package has no query surface for the one question a crew member actually asks a search tool ('where is symbol X, and who calls it'), only a whole-repo build plus a file-targeted slice. It cannot replace grep today, not because the data is missing but because the data is never published or persisted in a queryable form. Secondary risks: index.py is a 69k-char god-module, three planes (types, documents, wiki) are off by default, and structcore-rs is an unbuilt, untested-in-CI 6-of-18-language partial reimplementation with an honest but stale parity doc.

modules.plan_mapping: PRIOR section 5 (four-plane Project Twin) / Invariant 2 (artifact identity)
issues: Facade is incomplete and bypassed: it exports 7 of 24 modules; slice, graph, report, topology, churn, artifacts, lpg, cache, tokens are absent, so ~40 of ~47 external import sites reach past it into submodules (daedalus/web_api.py:34-38, daedalus/eval/harness.py:47-53, daedalus/ikarus_os.py:403-405). There is no single import surface a consumer can be held to.
Only two call sites use the facade at all (daedalus/mapping/render.py:589, daedalus/mapping/drift.py:1526, both `from daedalus.structcore import cached_index`), i.e. the facade is decorative.

modules.purpose: Builds the whole structural index: walk, scope, per-file analysis, clone passes, import/dep graph, fan_in, hotspots, plus the in-process index and resolver caches.
modules.plan_mapping: Gate 2 (Forest v2) foundation; PRIOR section 5 Code plane; Invariant 6 (atomic revisions)
issues: God-module: 69,099 chars / ~1250 lines carrying scoping (_View, _PyNaming, _py_dotted, _disambiguate, _scope_key), the parallel pass (_per_file_pass, _compute, _worker_count), three feature flags (documents/types/wiki), clone orchestration, graph folding and both caches. Every recent defect (G-01 fan_in alias split, G-02 center naming, G-03 junction walk) landed here, in different concerns.

The recent G-01 fix is correct and tested (tests/test_structcore_fanin_views.py) but the underlying design is the risk: dep_edges deliberately keeps two spellings per target (importer's-eye view) while fan_in folds them, so any future consumer of `dependencies` inherits the split identity that fan_in was just fixed for. index.py:718-721 documents the fold; nothing prevents a new reader of `dependencies` from re-introducing the double count.

`all_units` and `graph.name_index` (a global symbol->units map) are built at index.py:648-691 and 952 but never published in the returned dict (see the key list at index.py:1060-1121). The single most valuable retrieval primitive is computed and thrown away every scan.

Cache is in-process only (`_INDEX_CACHE`, index.py:1179; `_RESOLVER_CACHE`, index.py:1124). Only the per-file analyses persist (cache.py SQLite). A fresh `python -m daedalus.structcore` process re-folds the whole index; there is no persisted index artifact and no daemon, so a CLI-driven agent pays the fold on every question.
Types (index.py:217), documents (index.py:170) and wiki (index.py:238) are off by default, so the default index is a one-plane (Code) index, not the four-plane Twin the plan makes central.

docs.reason: The only document that describes the Python-vs-Rust divergence, and it is unusually honest about its own method (source reading, no build). Keep it as the authority for structcore-rs status; it needs a follow-up once a real differential run is possible.
Describes `center` and .daedalusignore, i.e. the ignore.py/index.py scoping semantics that G-02 just implemented. Slice-specific and current.

The design plan behind typegraph.py and markdown.py (Teil A / Teil B). Historical design authority for two modules of this slice; still the best statement of what the Type and Knowledge layers refuse to do.

Reports the typegraph build as 'built, tested, NOT committed (working tree only)' — stale: typegraph.py is committed and has 8 test files. The measurements are worth keeping; the status header must be superseded or the file folded into the plan doc as an appendix.

integration_gaps: No name-based query surface. `graph.name_index` (daedalus/structcore/graph.py:49) builds the global symbol->units map and `all_units` (index.py:648) holds every unit, but neither is published in the index dict (key list at index.py:1060-1121) or exposed on any CLI. Until a `structcore where <symbol>` / `callers <symbol>` verb exists, the crew cannot use structcore where they currently use grep — the answer is computed and discarded on every scan.

No persisted index artifact and no warm process. `_INDEX_CACHE` (index.py:1179) is in-process; only per-file analyses persist (cache.py). Every CLI invocation re-folds the index, and clone clustering is ~96% of that time (ignore.py:22-27). There is no `--no-clones` fast path, so the crew-facing entrypoint is minutes-scale where grep is milliseconds-scale.

Three of the four planes are not on by default. types (index.py:217) and documents (index.py:170) are flag-gated off, and artifacts.py (Data plane) has no index integration at all. Every default consumer — slice.py, graph_brief, web_api, dss/context_plan — therefore reasons over a Code-plane-only index, which is a live gap against the section 5 prior and Gate 2.

artifacts.py reaches production only through a swallowed `except ImportError: pass` at daedalus/eval/graph_delta.py:436, and only its literal extractor. If the import ever breaks, the Data-plane layer silently vanishes from the delta with no signal.

cycles.py and lpg.py are complete, tested and unreachable from any production caller — cycles.py is exported from the facade but imported by nothing outside tests; lpg.py only by a CLI flag. Both are wiring gaps rather than dead code.

Two divergent fan_in definitions coexist: the index's folded, center-aware one (index.py:889-907, fixed by G-01) and report.py:61-66's separately recomputed rel-keyed `graph_fan_in`. The G-01 identity fold does not apply to the second, so the CLI ranking and the web report can disagree on the same repo.

The facade (__init__.py) exports 7 of 24 modules while ~40 external import sites reach into submodules directly. There is no enforced public API, so any structcore refactor is a repo-wide breaking change with no compile-time signal.

structcore-rs has no CI build, no parity harness, and no caller. Its index shape is already known to diverge (missing total_tokens/tokenizer, 12 missing languages), and the divergence is handled by defensive `.get()` fallbacks in slice.py rather than by a version/producer field on the index dict.
notable: The gardener distillates are real, TDD'd, and measured, not cosmetic: tests/test_structcore_fanin_views.py encodes the G-01 defect with the actual repo numbers (75 split identities; structcore.parse listed twice at 13+12 instead of once at 25), and tests/test_structcore_center_naming.py encodes G-02 with the project_tct impact (87% of the code map isolated). Both tests assert the OLD behaviour is preserved for unscoped repos and pin determinism across PYTHONHASHSEED — this is the right shape for an identity-layer fix.

The refuse-not-guess discipline is consistent across the slice and is its strongest asset: fan_in collisions poison rather than bind (index.py, G-01), forest.py refuses to expand a clone group into a pairwise clique, lpg.py preserves that refusal and omits `plane` for unknown kinds rather than guessing, typegraph reports resolved/unresolved/ambiguous/external/builtin counts, and __main__.py prints scope/document/type withholding out loud. Under-report over invent is enforced by construction, not by convention.

ignore.py:41-56 documents the exact failure mode of a missed SCOPE_ALGO_SALT bump ('the fix did nothing', survives until restart, costs an afternoon). That comment is the kind of provenance the plan's Invariant 7 asks for — but the enforcement is still a human remembering to edit a constant, and the companion constant (perfile.ANALYSIS_VERSION) lives in a different file.

daedalus/lanes/graph_brief.py:3-17 records the measured root cause this whole slice exists to fix: 'the agents never see the graph' — no provider module referenced structcore, and a write lane hallucinated three symbol names that 6.5k characters of index output would have answered. graph_brief is the fix for write lanes; the crew's own read path (grep/Read) has no equivalent, which is precisely the question this slice was asked.

Verdict on the framing question: structcore is the right instrument for 'what is the shape of this neighborhood, what will I break, what is duplicated, what is hot' and it is materially better than grep at all four. It is not yet a substitute for grep on 'where is X' because it publishes no symbol index, persists no index, and has no query verbs — three additions (publish name_index in the index dict, persist the folded index keyed by scope_key, add `where`/`callers`/`cycles` verbs to __main__, plus a --no-clones fast build) would close the gap without any new subsystem, i.e. as pure wiring under the plan's section 14 preference.

Stale module docstring: daedalus/structcore/slice.py:13-15 still promises 'symbol-level precision arrives with graph.py (SCIP / stack-graphs)'. Neither SCIP nor stack-graphs exists in the repo; graph.py implements heuristic name resolution instead. A reader takes that line as a roadmap commitment.

daedalus/structcore/__init__.py:1-19 describes structcore as generalizing 'project_tct/TCT_app/tools/codemap.py' — an external repo path. Accurate as history, but the module head reads as if that file is the reference implementation, which is no longer true.

index.py is 69,099 chars and parse.py 55,796 — together 44% of the slice's Python by size. Both are imported directly by external consumers, so neither can be split without touching daedalus/eval/, daedalus/mapping/ and daedalus/web_api.py in the same change.
